clue.text: Garment missing last pocket

definitions.note: a verb: to take for yourself

indicators.note: missing its last means the final letter of the garment's name is dropped

blocks.note: a pair of trousers is a garment

explanation.surface: A pair of trousers that has lost its back pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pocket' looks like part of the garment, but it is the definition, a verb: to trouser money is to pocket it.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British usage, to trouser cash is to take it for yourself, exactly as one pockets it.

clue.text: Upper-class politician embraced by the Democrat gets beaten

indicators.note: embraced by means held within, so the class and politician go inside the following words

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the label for upper-class usage
Member of Parliament
the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A posh politician is hugged by a Democrat and then loses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets beaten' sounds like an election defeat, but it means physically struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Thumped means struck hard with the fist, a synonym for beaten.

clue.text: Dictionary includes daydreamer nearly missed out

indicators.note: includes means the dictionary holds the other piece within it
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

blocks.note: the Oxford English Dictionary
Walter Mitty, the fantasist of Thurber's story

explanation.surface: A dictionary nearly left out a word meaning daydreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Mitty is the fantasist in James Thurber's story 'The Secret Life of Walter Mitty', so his name stands for any daydreamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something omitted has been left out, the meaning of missed out.

clue.text: Look down on second growth on toe

blocks.note: the abbreviation for second
a corn is a hard growth on a toe

explanation.surface: Someone looks down at a second lump growing on the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look down on' invites a literal glance at a foot, but means despise.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn someone is to hold them in contempt, idiomatically to look down on them.

clue.text: Rest cue potting second of balls

indicators.note: second of means only the letter in position two is kept
potting means sinking something in a pocket, so the letter is pocketed inside the cue word

blocks.note: a cue is a prompt, a reminder
the second letter

explanation.surface: A snooker player's cue pots the next ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cue' and 'potting' paint a snooker table, but the cue is a prompt.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, a synonym for the rest.

clue.text: Expert recalled awful worker

indicators.note: recalled read as re-called, called back, so the word comes back the other way

blocks.note: awful means bad
a hand is a farm or factory worker

explanation.surface: A supposed expert is remembered as a dreadful employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is a British idiom for someone highly skilled at something.

clue.text: Training — this could be boring

blocks.note: first meaning: repetitive instruction, as in military exercise
second meaning: a tool for making holes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' seems to mean dull, which fits the training, but it means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers practise on the parade ground at drill, and the tool that bores through wood is a drill.

clue.text: Game birds — all I shot

indicators.note: shot means ruined or worn out, so the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A hunter boasts of shooting every game bird in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game birds' reads as pheasants and grouse; 'Game' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Billiards is a cue game played on a cloth table, an example of a game.

clue.text: A fit of anger after very little energy? That's mean, possibly

blocks.note: taken as written
v is the abbreviation for very
E is the symbol for energy
a rage is a fit of anger

explanation.surface: Losing your temper over a tiny lack of energy is unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' suggests unkind; it is the arithmetic sense, and 'possibly' flags that the mean is one kind of average.
explanation.definitionFit: The arithmetic mean is one type of average, hence the qualifier possibly.

clue.text: Drop old penny then pick up small European coin

indicators.note: pick up means lift, and lifting in a down answer turns the two letters upside down

blocks.note: d was the symbol for a pre-decimal penny
the abbreviation for small
the abbreviation for European
a cent is a coin

explanation.surface: Drop an old penny and then pick up a small euro coin.
explanation.walkthrough: D stood for an old British penny before 1971 decimalisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is a downward slope or fall, so it is a noun synonym for a drop.

clue.text: Fixed costume

blocks.note: first meaning: constant, the same throughout
second meaning: a standard outfit worn by members of a group

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a costume that has been repaired; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means unvarying; as a noun it is the regulation dress of a school, team or force.

clue.text: Complaint from this writer will regularly incense readers, ultimately

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter of incense is kept
ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter of readers counts

blocks.note: the setter says I'll, I will
the second, fourth and sixth letters
the last letter

explanation.surface: The setter predicts that a provocative grumble will annoy readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is the setter, I, so 'this writer will' contracts to I'LL.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is a medical ailment, so it is a synonym for a sickness.

clue.text: Latin poet's broken promise

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so the letters are put back in a different order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A Roman poet failed to keep his word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken promise' reads as a phrase, but 'broken' belongs to the wordplay and 'promise' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing promise means having latent ability that may develop, which is the noun's meaning.

clue.text: Rodent inside that is foaming at the mouth

indicators.note: inside places the rodent within the other piece, enclosed by it

blocks.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A rabid rat is frothing at the lips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foaming at the mouth' suggests rabies, but here it is the figurative sense of fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone foaming at the mouth is livid with anger, the idiom for being furious.

clue.text: Duck departs house in the wilds, wanting lake

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the house loses the letter for lake

blocks.note: d. is the abbreviation for departs in timetables
a lodge is a cabin in remote country
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A duck leaves a remote cabin that has no water nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird, but it is the verb meaning to evade.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question is to evade it, a synonym of the verb meaning to sidestep.

clue.text: Large mammals from Hampshire with Brazilian footballer mounted on top

indicators.note: mounted means climbing upwards, and in a down answer that sends the name backwards

blocks.note: Pele, the famous Brazilian striker
Hants is the abbreviation for the English county of Hampshire

explanation.surface: Big beasts from Hampshire carry a Brazilian football star on their backs.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county in southern England, abbreviated HANTS; the reversed footballer sits on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants are the largest living land mammals.

clue.text: Cleaner put off by grand hospital department

blocks.note: to deter is to put off
G is short for grand, a thousand
ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A cleaner feels discouraged by a large hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a chemical cleaning agent, as in washing-up liquid.

clue.text: Great help untangling wire

indicators.note: untangling means sorting out a knot, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is a big help in sorting out a knotted cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wire' is the old word for a telegram or the telegraph itself, and also names this newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire was a telegram, sent by telegraph; to wire someone was to telegraph them.

clue.text: Heard cat moving in front of large church

indicators.note: moving letters shifts them around into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
L is the abbreviation for large on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone heard a cat prowling in front of a big church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large church' looks like the definition, but 'large' supplies the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, housing the bishop's throne.

clue.text: Rushes jobs

blocks.note: first meaning: hurtles along out of control
second meaning: lifelong professions

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it is hasty work; the two words are separate meanings, a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A car careers down a hill when it rushes wildly; careers are also occupations followed for life.

clue.text: Proclaim election trickery, initially, supporting former president

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so only the first letters of the two words are taken

blocks.note: Donald Trump, a former US president
the first letters of both words

explanation.surface: Someone loudly alleges vote-rigging in defence of an ex-president.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'supporting' means placed below, so the initials come after the president.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to announce it loudly, as a herald's fanfare would.

clue.text: Venom from wasp — it evolves, to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent means only partly, so the answer is a part of the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters across the words

explanation.surface: The sting of a wasp has developed over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venom' looks like poison, but it means malice.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is figuratively bitter malice, which is a synonym for spite.

clue.text: Passionate campers could be here, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the answer is heard rather than spelt like the phrase

blocks.note: campers sleep under canvas

explanation.surface: Keen campers might be found pitched here, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense feelings are strong and ardent, a synonym for passionate.

clue.text: Eternal idleness at sea? Not I!

indicators.note: at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are in disorder
Not I tells you to remove the letter I from the word

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An everlasting lazy cruise — but not for me!
explanation.definitionFit: Something endless never stops, which is a synonym for everlasting.

clue.text: Violent brother scratching head? That's disgusting

indicators.note: scratching means striking out, so the head, the first letter, is removed

blocks.note: bro is short for brother
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A brute of a sibling scratches his scalp, to general revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough play is violent, so the adjective is a synonym for using force.

clue.text: Ignored information about the French editor outside court

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for information runs backwards
outside means the French word and editor wrap around the abbreviation for court

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
le is French for the
the abbreviation for court
the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A French newspaper editor's report about a court case was disregarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it turns the slang word round; 'the French' and 'editor' then wrap the court.
explanation.definitionFit: Something neglected has been left unattended, a synonym for being ignored.

clue.text: Terrible ink's inside a pen

indicators.note: inside means the innermost part, so only the central letter is kept

blocks.note: the middle letter
taken as written
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: There is awful ink in a fountain pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool next to 'ink', but it is an enclosure for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty means very bad or unpleasant, so it is a synonym for terrible.

clue.text: Mistake some juror regretfully brought up

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the answer is a stretch of the following words
brought up means raised, and in a down answer rising letters read in reverse

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A juror sorrowfully raises a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, a straightforward synonym for a slip.

clue.text: Former lover with son eats quietly and gets bigger

indicators.note: eats means the outer pieces swallow what follows, holding it inside

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
p, piano, means quietly in music
and means with
the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An ex-partner and her son eat silently and put on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is easy to read as a link, but it is a piece; the former lover and son together swallow 'quietly and'.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand is to swell or increase in size, so the verb means grows larger.

clue.text: Sort out a Republican row

blocks.note: taken as written
the abbreviation for Republican
a range is a row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: Resolving a dispute with a member of the Republican party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it means a line, as in a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things is to put them in order, a synonym for sorting them out.

clue.text: Meet heads of state attending talks involving San Franciscan youths

indicators.note: heads are tops, so the first letter of each following word is taken

blocks.clueFragment: state attending talks involving San Franciscan youths
blocks.note: the opening letters of seven words

explanation.surface: World leaders attend a summit about young Californians.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a requirement is to fulfil it, a synonym for satisfying it.

clue.text: Control and make use of gear

blocks.note: first meaning: to exploit a resource, as with power
second meaning: the straps and fittings of a horse

explanation.walkthrough: The verb is to harness energy; the noun is a horse's tack or a climber's straps.
explanation.definitionFit: One harnesses the wind to use it, and a harness is the equipment, or gear, fastened onto a horse.
